messages.content: How to get nodes information for fabric test-de, the ip is 23.31.32.1?

function.name: telemetry_flowrules_interfaceInfo_get
function.description: Retrieves specified telemetry information for a network interface within a given fabric, node, and pod, filtered by the interface and information types. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit the nodes pertaining to the given fabric name.

nodeId.description: The identifier of the node to limit the results pertaining to the given node ID.

podId.description: The identifier of the pod to limit the results pertaining to the given pod ID.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit the results pertaining to the given interface type.

infoType.description: The type of information to retrieve about the interface.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide showing **how** you’d pull the list of nodes that belong to the *test‑de* fabric from a switch whose management IP is 23.31.32.1.  
(If your environment uses a different base URL or auth scheme just swap those parts out.)

---

### 1️⃣ Build the HTTP request

| Element | What goes here |
|---------|----------------|
| Base URL | `http://<switch-ip>/api/v1/telemetry` – replace `<switch-ip>` with **23.31.32.1** |
| Endpoint | `/nodes` – gives you the full node inventory |
| Query params | `?fabric=test-de` – limits the result set to the “test‑de” fabric |

Putting it together:

```
curl -k \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -u <username>:<password> \   # <-- basic auth; adjust per your setup
     "https://23.31.32.1/api/v1/telemetry/nodes?fabric=test-de"
```

> **Tip:**  
> • Replace `-k` with proper TLS verification once you’ve installed the correct cert.  
> • If you’re using OAuth2 bearer tokens instead of Basic Auth, change the header line to:
>
> ```
> -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN_HERE"
> ```

---

### 2️⃣ Expected JSON shape

```json
{
  "fabric": "test-de",
  "totalNodes": 12,
  "nodes": [
    {
      "id": 101,
      "hostname": "leaf01.test-de.local",
      "role": "Leaf",
      "ipAddress": "10.0.0.101",
      "model": "Nexus9000 C9300v",
      ...
    },
    { ... }
  ]
}
```

Each entry under `"nodes"` contains everything you’ll typically care about—ID, hostname, role, IP, platform details, software version, uptime, etc.  

---

### 3️⃣ Filtering further (optional)

If you only want nodes that expose a certain feature or meet a condition, most APIs let you add extra filters:

```
.../nodes?fabric=test-de&role=Leaf&softwareVersion>=9.3.5
```

Check your vendor’s docs for supported query keys (`role`, `platform`, `uptime`, …).

---

### 4️⃣ Using the SDK / library (Python example)

If you prefer code over raw `cURL`, many vendors ship a lightweight client. Here’s a minimal snippet assuming a simple requests wrapper exists:

```python
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://23.31.32.1/api/v1/telemetry"
HEADERS = {"Accept": "application/json"}
AUTH = ("admin", "P@ssw0rd")          # or token-based auth

resp = requests.get(
    f"{BASE_URL}/nodes",
    headers=HEADERS,
    params={"fabric": "test-de"},
    auth=AUTH,
    verify=False                      # skip SSL check for demo purposes
)
data = resp.json()
print(f"There are {len(data['nodes'])} nodes in fabric '{data['fabric']}'.")
for n in data["nodes"]:
    print(n["hostname"], n["ipAddress"])
```

Replace `verify=False` with a real CA bundle when moving to production.

---

#### Bottom line

Your goal is simply to hit the **“list nodes”** telemetry endpoint while scoping the request to the desired fabric. Once you have that payload, you can parse whatever fields you need downstream. Happy querying!
